title: Marmont to Jourdan, 1812 (catalogue 751) and Jourdan to Soult, 28 May 1812, in the Grand Chiffre of 1812; Jardet to Marmont (724) already deciphered

plaintext.source: Contemporary Spanish translation of the plain parts; the cipher numbers were left undeciphered.

transcription.notes: Copy by a Spanish clerk; a few digits doubtful.

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the AHN copy; a manuscript decipherment by Scovell is reported (Oman), not printed.
Existing: the piece is a "copia descifrada conforme" with the key attached (image 11).

system.summary: Grand Chiffre of 1812 (the British “Great Paris Cipher”): a repertory of 1,200 numbers (letters, syllables, words) extended to 1,400 with additions for Spain (1211 = the Army of the Centre, 1214 = the English army, 1300 = Lord Wellington, 1383 = the Tagus); several numbers for frequent words (homophones)

prior_solution.where: N.73 (751): Scovell's manuscript decipherment (Oman V app. XV no. 28), not printed. N.34: not in the Scovell list; not printed in Du Casse (Mémoires du roi Joseph IX), Marmont's Mémoires IV, Jourdan's Mémoires militaires, Wellington's Dispatches IX or Supplementary Despatches VII (searched 28 Oct 2026). N.29 (724): contemporary Spanish decipherment in the piece.

texts.label: Jourdan to Soult, Madrid, 28 May 1812 (AHN DIVERSOS-COLECCIONES,134,N.34)
texts.summary: Eight weeks before the battle of Salamanca, Marshal Jourdan, King Joseph’s chief of staff, orders Soult to reinforce Count d’Erlon’s corps against General Hill, or to send it across the Tagus at the bridge of the Arzobispo if Wellington calls Hill back to him. The letter was intercepted: a contemporary Spanish translation survives in the Archivo Histórico Nacional, with the enciphered passages left as numbers, undeciphered. They read with the table of the 1812 Grand Chiffre.
